correctness.rationale: For each integer k=4..8, the delivered standard-library verifier exhaustively enumerates all independent k-sets of Q4, constructs every nonempty simplex via facets and independently via a correct include/exclude independence-number DP, checks set equality, matches faces by vertex stages, orients every Hasse cover and topologically sorts all vertices of the oriented matching graph. Exact critical cells: k4 one vertex plus 529 eight-cells; k5 plus 937 six-cells; k6 plus 441 four-cells; k7 plus 49 two-cells; k8 two vertices. Counts and pair digests match the delivered certificate. Theorem 7.5 of Bayer et al. also establishes staged matching acyclicity. Forman discrete-Morse theory converts exactly these critical cells to the asserted integral sphere wedges. All cases are finite and exhaustive.

evidence: Carnero Bravo, arxiv:2602.21427v3, Question 53, explicitly asks for the higher-d total cut complexes of Cartesian products of complete graphs; Theorem 52 concerns only d=2.

Bayer et al., arxiv:2209.13503v2, pp. 10-21, provide formulas for complete bipartite graphs, cycles, grid families at k=2, and tables for rectangular grids; they do not give the k=4..8 four-cube tower.
Chauhan-Shukla-Vinayak, arxiv:2512.04486, p. 1-3, give theorems on total 2-cut for Cartesian products and discuss conjectures for higher cuts in other graph families.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The most plausible dominating theorems examined do not cover Q4 at k=4..8. The 2026 explicit open question is stronger evidence of an unresolved general family, but not by itself proof that every finite specialization is absent.

value.rationale: Q4 is the first fourfold binary Cartesian complete-graph product, a canonical 16-vertex symmetric object. k=4..8 is the entire remaining nonvoid high-cut interval rather than a chosen arbitrary slice; it provides exact homotopy types, including the 8-to-0 sphere-dimension transition, and complete torsion-free homology. The theorem addresses a natural finite specialization of a published open question on higher cuts of Cartesian complete-graph products (Carnero Bravo 2026, Question 53). It makes no paper-size or general-dimension claim and the natural cutoff alpha(Q4)=8 is proven.
